import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Ensure 'data/iris.csv' exists. Using seaborn's built-in iris dataset as a fallback.")
    df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

# Set a professional and visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a pair plot to visualize pairwise relationships and distributions
# This is an excellent choice for this dataset because it allows us to see
# how the species are separated by each combination of features.
g = sns.pairplot(
    df,
    hue='species',
    diag_kind='kde',
    markers=["o", "s", "D"],
    plot_kws={'alpha': 0.8, 's': 60, 'edgecolor': 'k'},
    diag_kws={'fill': True}
)

# Add a clear, descriptive title to the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    "Distribution and Relationship of Iris Flower Features by Species",
    y=1.03, # Position title slightly above the plot
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight='bold'
)

# Improve readability of axis labels by adding units (assuming cm)
for ax in g.axes.flatten():
    if ax.get_xlabel() in df.columns:
        ax.set_xlabel(ax.get_xlabel().replace('_', ' ').title() + ' (cm)')
    if ax.get_ylabel() in df.columns:
        ax.set_ylabel(ax.get_ylabel().replace('_', ' ').title() + ' (cm)')

# Adjust legend title
g.legend.set_title("Species")

import pandas as pd

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    print("Ensure 'data/iris.csv' exists. Using seaborn's built-in iris dataset as a fallback.")
    df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

# Set a professional and visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a pair plot to visualize pairwise relationships and distributions
# This is an excellent choice for this dataset because it allows us to see
# how the species are separated by each combination of features.
g = sns.pairplot(
    df,
    hue='species',
    diag_kind='kde',
    markers=["o", "s", "D"],
    plot_kws={'alpha': 0.8, 's': 60, 'edgecolor': 'k'},
    diag_kws={'fill': True}
)

# Add a clear, descriptive title to the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    "Distribution and Relationship of Iris Flower Features by Species",
    y=1.03, # Position title slightly above the plot
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight='bold'
)

# Improve readability of axis labels by adding units (assuming cm)
for ax in g.axes.flatten():
    if ax.get_xlabel() in df.columns:
        ax.set_xlabel(ax.get_xlabel().replace('_', ' ').title() + ' (cm)')
    if ax.get_ylabel() in df.columns:
        ax.set_ylabel(ax.get_ylabel().replace('_', ' ').title() + ' (cm)')

# Adjust legend title
